findings.decisive_evidence: 2E-K >=43*pi/1400>0. Actual curve length (4/5)K <=4*pi/7<pi. Every printed family member has unit speed and length 2NK>pi. Isometry and full reparametrisation cannot change length. Independently, printed N scaling changes multiplier to lambda/N^2.
findings.proof: Full analytic proof in report Sections 3.1-3.2; rational checks independently executed in independent_checks.py. The rational computation alone is not the stationarity proof.
findings.impact: Additional pinned classification is false as printed. problems.reasoning: Independently checked gamma_w unit-speed scaling and endpoint natural boundary conditions from (2.2). At m=51/100, a=1/5 and lambda=1, the shifted repeated wave has zero curvature at both endpoints, multiplier (4m-2)/a^2=1, endpoint separation 4a(2E-K)>0 and length 4aK<=4pi/7. Integral bounds give 2E-K>=43pi/1400. Every printed unit-speed family member has length 2NK>pi, so isometry or full reparametrization cannot supply this pinned critical curve. Also the printed N-dependent spatial scaling gives multiplier lambda/N^2. The repaired [0,2NaK] family and retained absolute-value endpoint equation have matching dimensions and stationarity. The defect concerns the supplementary pinned classification; the adjacent Theorem4.1/Corollary4.2 and Theorem4.4 use the correct multiplier scaling, so no central failure is established.
problems.counterevidence: The original endpoint equation does contain absolute-value bars; the current report already withdraws that old extraction-based allegation. Central uniqueness claims are not refuted by the local counterexample.
problems.repair_scope: Correct repeated-wave family verified; root-count and zero-distance assertions remain outside this focused acceptance.
